record.narrative: The due validations close the last two credible discovery leads. H113, the outcome_012 feature_057 level-10 versus level-2 contrast, had a signed discovery estimate of +0.0256, narrowly above the roughly 0.025 clinical-magnitude proxy, with discovery interval [0.0044, 0.0468]. However, the independent validation estimate R100 is only +0.0036 with interval [-0.0282, 0.0354], essentially null and far below the clinical reference; combined evidence does not credibly establish a clinically meaningful association, so H113 is rejected and closed. H58, outcome_005 feature_065=1 versus 0, had a subthreshold discovery signed estimate of +0.0155 with interval [-0.0037, 0.0348], and the independent validation R101 is opposite to the registered direction and null, -0.0116 with interval [-0.0402, 0.0171]. There is no reason to retain it as a candidate, so H58 is rejected and closed. The supported scientific conclusion remains negative: across a broad screen of common binary predictors, categorical contrasts, discrete feature_057 dose contrasts, and multiple predictor-outcome panels, no measured predictor or subgroup shows a robust clinically meaningful difference in these CRISPR dependency outcomes. This is not proof that no association exists; it is the strongest conclusion supported by the data. The repeated collapse of near-threshold discovery estimates in independent validation or cross-outcome replication is consistent with winner's-curse effects under high multiplicity. I am retaining H43 as unresolved active because it is the only remaining near-threshold outlier: outcome_011 feature_028 level_003 versus level_002 has a signed estimate of +0.0427, above the roughly 0.030 outcome_011 clinical-magnitude proxy, but its interval includes null and clinically smaller effects and the comparison may have been shaped after inspecting the companion H21 result. A single targeted validation or pre-specified replication of H43 would be the most informative next follow-up if validation capacity is available. H145 and H148 are low-prior completion items and are deferred so that any remaining capacity can focus on the one high-magnitude unresolved candidate. No new validated claims are accepted; all statements are observational and specific to the supplied dataset.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No accepted claims currently exist, and the existing evidence is dominated by null, subthreshold, or winner's-curse-like near-threshold findings. The only retained near-threshold discovery candidate is H43, outcome_011 feature_028 level_003 versus level_002, whose signed estimate exceeds the roughly 0.030 absolute mean-scale clinical reference but whose interval includes null and clinically smaller effects. Because the comparator is rare, direct or independent validation is expected to remain imprecise. The most informative next step is therefore a pre-specified follow-up of the feature_028 level pattern in outcome_011: test level_003 versus level_001, level_001 versus level_002, and level_004 versus level_002. If H43 reflects a real level effect, level_003 or one of the nonreference levels should show a coherent pattern of stronger dependency; if it is a post-hoc rare-cell artifact, the other contrasts should be mixed or null. This panel is linked to H43 but changes the comparison rather than reversing it. I also register two high-power interaction contrasts among the balanced binary predictors on outcome_012, where absolute means are relatively small and cells are large: feature_034 modified by feature_060 and feature_060 modified by feature_002. Null main effects do not preclude effect modification, but prior effect-modification searches have failed; these are therefore exploratory but scientifically meaningful tests of whether dependency differences are additive or condition-dependent. Finally, I register main-effect completion contrasts for outcome_011 feature_002 and feature_060, outcome_008 feature_034, feature_060, and feature_045, and outcome_006 feature_045 and feature_042. These cover remaining common binary predictors in outcomes with clinically interpretable reference magnitudes. The registered direction is negative in each main-effect or interaction claim, so a positive returned estimate means stronger dependency under the registered exposed contrast. Anticipated directions are mostly zero because the predictor labels are opaque and previous screens for these predictors were null; the feature_028 level_003 versus level_001 contrast is the only one with an expected negative raw contrast based on the H43 lead. Acceptance still requires a signed estimate reaching approximately 10 percent of the absolute outcome mean with uncertainty that credibly excludes smaller effects. These analyses are observational and remain limited to the supplied dataset.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All returned estimates are already signed to the registered direction, so positive values mean stronger dependency under the exposed contrast and negative values mean weaker dependency under that contrast. The outcome_011 feature_028 level panel gives a cautiously more coherent pattern around the retained H43 lead. H153, level_003 versus level_001, is essentially null: estimate -0.0012, interval [-0.0459, 0.0435]. This rejects a simple pattern in which only level_003 differs from all other common levels. However, H154, level_001 versus level_002, estimate +0.0438, interval [-0.0177, 0.1054], and H155, level_004 versus level_002, estimate +0.0427, interval [-0.0112, 0.0965], both show positive signed contrasts of nearly the same magnitude as H43. Together with H43, this is consistent with level_002 having weaker dependency than levels_001/003/004, rather than a random rare-cell artifact. The panel is not sufficient for acceptance: H154 and H155 have rare-cell comparisons and wide intervals that include null and clinically smaller effects, and all three contrasts are dependent observations on the same outcome and predictor. They therefore justify targeted validation of the original H43 contrast, not direct acceptance of any single panel contrast. I reject H153 because it is null and does not support a level_003-specific effect; I keep H154 and H155 unresolved and active as supporting panel evidence while H43 is validated. The outcome_012 interaction screen is negative. H156, feature_034 modified by feature_060, has estimate -0.0141, interval [-0.0456, 0.0175], well below the roughly 0.025 outcome_012 mean-scale clinical proxy and imprecise. H157, feature_060 modified by feature_002, has estimate +0.0161, interval [-0.0155, 0.0477], also subthreshold and null-compatible. These do not support robust effect modification and are closed. The main-effect completion screen is mostly uninformative: H158 outcome_011 feature_002 estimate -0.0126, H159 outcome_011 feature_060 estimate +0.0072, H160 outcome_008 feature_034 estimate +0.0106, H161 outcome_008 feature_060 estimate -0.0064, H162 outcome_008 feature_045 estimate -0.0175, and H164 outcome_006 feature_042 estimate +0.0078 are either clearly below the relevant outcome-specific 10% mean-scale proxies or have intervals compatible with no clinically meaningful effect. These are rejected and closed. H163 is the only main-effect completion candidate that is materially above its outcome-specific clinical proxy: outcome_006 feature_045, estimate +0.0314, interval [-0.0043, 0.0670]. The point estimate is well above the roughly 0.009 outcome_006 absolute-mean reference, but the 95% interval includes zero and clinically smaller effects, and this is a single unreplicated screen result after extensive multiplicity. It therefore remains unresolved and active as a secondary near-threshold candidate, but I do not request validation for it now because H43 has more internal coherence across a pre-specified level panel and a more specific competing artifact story. I request independent validation of H43, outcome_011 feature_028 level_003 versus level_002, because it is the original high-magnitude lead and the best-powered contrast in the panel. If validation replicates a clinically meaningful signed effect with tighter uncertainty, acceptance could become defensible; if validation is null or opposite, the entire feature_028 outcome_011 lead should be closed as winner's-curse or rare-level noise. If H43 fails, H163 would be the next most plausible near-threshold candidate, although its prior probability remains low given the broad multiplicity. H43 direction -1 had a discovery signed estimate of +0.0427 with an interval that still included null and clinically smaller effects, and the independent validation signed estimate is only +0.0251 with interval [-0.0412, 0.0914] at the stringent independent alpha. The validation point is below the roughly 0.030 absolute mean-scale 10% reference for outcome_011 and is far too imprecise to support a clinically meaningful negative-direction claim, so H43 is rejected and closed. The companion level contrasts H154 and H155 showed coherent positive signed contrasts around the original H43 lead, but both are rare-cell comparisons with wide intervals and now lack the validation support that would have made the pattern credible; therefore they are also rejected as unsupported and closed. H137 remains rejected and closed because its validation signed estimate is -0.0250 with interval [-0.0715, 0.0215], opposite to the registered negative direction and null-compatible. The same evidence for the reversed claim H138 is positive, with signed discovery and validation estimates around +0.0298 and +0.0250, near the roughly 0.025 clinical proxy for outcome_012 and replicated in direction. This is the strongest residual effect-modification signal, but the intervals still include zero and clinically smaller or opposite effects, so it is not accepted; I reassess it as unresolved and active. H163 remains unresolved and active: the discovery signed estimate is +0.0314 with interval [-0.0043, 0.0670], a large apparent relative effect for outcome_006 but still unvalidated and imprecise. This is not proof that no associations exist; it is the most defensible conclusion from the supplied observational dataset, with winner's-curse-like attenuation across validation. The most informative next analyses are targeted rather than broad: decompose H138 into feature_002 subgroup mean differences to determine whether the interaction is localized and clinically meaningful, and pursue confirmation or independent validation for the H163 outcome_006 feature_045 candidate. record.narrative: No assessments are due because this form requests analyses rather than appraising newly returned results. I selected twelve already registered, untested, active claims that are maximally informative for the two residual near-threshold leads, rather than expanding the broad screen. The first block decomposes the H138/H137 feature_002-by-feature_034 interaction signal for outcome_012: H165 and H166 give the subgroup mean differences in feature_002=1 and feature_002=0; H174 and H175 provide marginal feature_002 and feature_060 context for outcome_012; and H177 tests a related feature_002-by-feature_034 interaction under a positive direction. This should distinguish a localized but meaningful feature_034 effect in one feature_002 stratum from a diffuse interaction artifact, while also checking whether marginal baseline differences could generate an apparently large interaction with wide subgroup intervals. The second block tests the unvalidated H163 lead for outcome_006 feature_045: H167-H169 decompose feature_045 by feature_002 and feature_034, H170-H172 test feature_034 as a possible modifier, and H173 uses outcome_014 as a closely matched triangulation outcome. If feature_045 has a genuine stronger-dependency signal on outcome_006, we expect a raw exposed-minus-comparator effect to move the score more negative, yielding positive signed estimates under the registered negative-direction claims, across at least some balanced strata and ideally in the outcome_014 triangulation. If the estimates are inconsistent, confined to one stratum, subclinical by the outcome-specific mean-scale 10% reference, or fail outcome_014 triangulation, H163 should be closed rather than validated. These estimates will remain signed to the registered hypothesis directions, so positive values indicate stronger dependency for the exposed-minus-comparator or interaction contrast under the corresponding negative-direction claims, whereas positive values for positive-direction claims also indicate the asserted direction. The analyses are confirmatory follow-ups in the supplied dataset; they do not establish causality or generalizability.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All returned estimates are already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For the negative-direction feature_045 claims, positive signed values mean the raw exposed-minus-comparator dependency score is more negative, i.e. feature_045=1 is associated with stronger dependency on outcome_006; for the positive-direction outcome_012 feature_034/feature_002 claims, positive signed values mean the raw contrast is in the asserted direction. No evidence supports accepting any claim outright at this stage. The most important negative result is that the H138 outcome_012 feature_034-by-feature_002 interaction does not survive decomposition. H165 in feature_002=1 is only +0.0123 with interval [-0.0104, 0.0351], and H166 in feature_002=0 is -0.0175 with interval [-0.0395, 0.0044]; both are clinically small under any reasonable mean-scale proxy and H166 is opposite the positive claim. The H138/H177 interaction point estimates are near the generous outcome_012 clinical proxy, but they are derived from opposite small subgroup contrasts rather than from large stratum-specific effects, and both discovery and validation intervals include zero and clinically smaller or opposite effects. Given the enormous multiplicity and the prior validation attenuation across the run, I reject and close H138 and the adjacent unvalidated H177 rather than accept a near-threshold interaction artifact. The null/low-support main-effect contexts H174 and H175 are also rejected and closed because they do not explain the interaction as a strong marginal baseline difference. The feature_045 block for outcome_006 is more internally coherent. The main effect H163 has a large positive signed point estimate, +0.0314, although the interval includes null and clinically smaller effects. The feature_002 stratum contrasts H167 and H168 and the feature_034 stratum contrasts H170 and H171 all point in the same stronger-dependency direction, while the interaction terms H169 and H172 are imprecise and null-compatible, which is more consistent with a main effect than with robust effect modification. However, this remains a post-screen subgroup decomposition with very wide intervals, and the pre-specified triangulation outcome_014 H173 is opposite in sign and null-compatible, so H163 cannot be accepted. I keep H163 active and request independent validation because it is the only remaining unvalidated candidate with both a high-magnitude point estimate and directional coherence across several balanced strata. H168 and H170 are the strongest supporting stratum contrasts and remain active pending validation, but they are not accepted. H173 is rejected and closed because it fails triangulation and does not support the feature_045 hypothesis. The interactions H169 and H172 are rejected and closed because they do not establish meaningful effect modification. Overall, the critical review does not reveal leakage or invalid Welch cells; all reported cells meet the minimum cell-size rule. The main threats are selection/multiplicity, winner's-curse attenuation, dependence among outcome and predictor screens, and the fact that these are observational comparisons only. Independent validation of H163 is therefore the most useful next evidence; a positive validation interval excluding null and exceeding the clinical threshold would make H163 acceptable as a dataset-specific association, while null, opposite, or subthreshold validation would close the feature_045 lead and leave the broad screen without robust accepted findings.

record.narrative: The scheduled validation for H163 closes the last feature_045 lead. H163 tested the negative-direction claim that feature_045=1 is associated with a more negative outcome_006 dependency score than feature_045=0. Discovery gave a positive signed estimate of +0.0314 with 95% interval [-0.0043, 0.0670], which was large relative to the 10% absolute-mean-scale proxy for outcome_006 (about 0.009), but it was not statistically secure. The independent validation estimate was -0.0033 with interval [-0.0577, 0.0510] at the stringent validation alpha; because the estimate is signed to the registered direction, this means the raw contrast was essentially null and numerically opposite the claimed stronger-dependency direction, with magnitude far below the clinical proxy. I therefore reject H163 as unsupported and close it. The supporting feature_002 and feature_034 stratum contrasts H167, H168, H170, and H171 are also rejected and closed: their positive point estimates were imprecise and were retained only as possible confirmation of the now-failed H163 lead. H176, an untested outcome_012 feature_045-by-feature_002 interaction refinement, is closed with investigation-only change because it was tied to the same unsupported predictor lead. There are no accepted claims. The strongest scientific conclusion supported by this dataset is that the broad exploratory screen did not identify any measured predictor or subgroup comparison that is robustly associated with scientifically meaningful differences in these CRISPR dependency scores. Several discovery leads that looked large, including feature_028 level_002 versus level_003 for outcome_011, feature_057 dose contrasts for outcome_012, the outcome_006 feature_045 lead, and the outcome_012 feature_034-by-feature_002 interaction, attenuated, reversed, or failed to become localized in a clinically meaningful stratum. The interaction screen is especially informative because its decomposition into feature_002 subgroup mean differences showed small or opposite stratum contrasts rather than a large subgroup-specific effect. Common binary predictors, most categorical contrasts, and the feature_034/feature_002/feature_060 interaction family produced mostly null effects or intervals dominated by uncertainty. These are dataset-specific observational findings; they do not establish causality or generalizability and do not prove the absence of true effects. Some untested or deferred contrasts remain, and validation intervals can be wide, so precise null claims are not warranted. The most informative next step would not be another post-hoc fishing sweep of the same predictors. If further work is performed, it should be either a tightly prespecified, well-powered test of a new biologically motivated predictor or a calibration or negative-control analysis to characterize the false-positive and attenuation behavior of this multiplicity-rich discovery-validation process. Otherwise, the report should emphasize the negative evidence and the failure of near-threshold leads to replicate.

record.narrative: The accepted set remains empty after many closed near leads, so the next comparisons should be focused triangulation tests of the one predictor family that still has a non-null direct discovery signal rather than another broad sweep. Feature_048 level_001 versus level_003 is the candidate: on outcome_015 (R31, direction -1) the signed effect was positive and the interval excluded zero, meaning the raw exposed-minus-comparator score was more negative, consistent with stronger dependency, but the magnitude was below the absolute 10%-of-mean clinical proxy for that outcome. On outcome_001 (R16) the same contrast had a larger point estimate in the same raw-negative direction but was imprecise. These two related outcomes are the only feature_048 leads not tied to closed predictor families such as feature_045, feature_057, feature_028, or the feature_034-by-feature_002 interaction family. I register outcome_013 as an independent outcome triangulation because its dependency-score scale is similar to outcome_015 but it was not used to form the original feature_048 lead, and I register outcome_014 because its smaller absolute mean gives a lower 10%-of-mean proxy, so a similar raw effect could be clinically meaningful there if it is real and not outcome-specific noise. I also register a balanced median split of feature_024 as a modifier to test whether the feature_048 effect is diluted across the full population or concentrated in a biologically plausible stratum; feature_024 is fully observed, has adequate cells after median split, and is not part of the earlier closed interaction leads. For all feature_048 claims, direction -1 encodes the hypothesis that level_001 is associated with more negative scores than level_003, i.e. stronger dependency; the returned signed estimates will be positive if the raw contrast is negative. A genuine feature_048 association should therefore produce raw-negative or signed-positive effects on outcome_013 or outcome_014 and, if diluted, should show a stronger feature_048 effect in one feature_024 stratum than the complement. If all triangulation and modifier contrasts are null, subclinical, or opposite, this would justify closing feature_048 as another discovery-only lead. If one untested outcome or subgroup gives a clinically sized signed-positive effect with reasonably tight uncertainty, it would be worth requesting independent validation before acceptance. These are observational dataset-specific associations only; they do not establish causality or generalizability.

record.narrative: All due results were interpreted using the already signed estimates: for direction -1 claims, positive signed values mean the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is in the hypothesized more-negative/stronger-dependency direction, while negative signed values mean the raw contrast is opposite. H178 is weakly in the hypothesized direction but has a point estimate below the outcome_013 mean-scale 10% proxy and an interval that includes zero, opposite, and clinically larger values; it does not triangulate the feature_048 lead. H179 has a point estimate above the small outcome_014 mean-scale proxy, but the interval is null-compatible and opposite-compatible, and the surrounding feature_048 evidence is inconsistent; it is rejected and closed. The feature_024 median-split tests reveal why: H180 is essentially null in feature_024 >= -7.353, while H181 is significantly opposite the registered direction in feature_024 <= -7.353, with raw effect approximately level_001 minus level_003 = +0.042, i.e. level_001 is associated with a less negative outcome_015 score in that subgroup. This exceeds the outcome_015 10% mean-scale proxy at the point estimate, although the lower bound is still subclinical. Thus the original H181 claim is rejected, but it is the only new signal worth independent validation because it is stratum-localized and clinically sized. H182 is nominally significant in the registered interaction direction, but that result is driven mainly by the opposite H181 stratum effect and by a null H180 stratum effect; its lower bound is below the clinical threshold and effect-modification claims are highly prone to multiplicity, so it remains unresolved rather than accepted. H183 and H184 provide no outcome_001 support for the feature_048/feature_024 pattern and are rejected and closed. The residual common-binary outcome_012 screen (H119, H120, H121, H126, H127) is also null, opposite, or subclinical and is closed. I request validation of H181 to test whether the stratum-specific feature_048 association replicates; if validation supports a robust raw-positive/signed-negative effect, I will consider a reversed proposal rather than accepting H181 itself.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The validation evidence for the remaining active feature_048 leads closes the last substantive predictor family without supporting any claim. H43 tested outcome_011 feature_028 level_003 versus level_002 in the claimed stronger-dependency direction. Discovery had a borderline positive signed estimate (+0.043; interval about [-0.004, +0.090]), but independent validation gave only +0.025 with a wide independent interval [-0.041, +0.091] that crosses zero and has a point estimate below the approximate 10%-of-absolute-mean clinical scale for outcome_011. This is inconsistent and unsupported, so H43 remains rejected and closed. H181 originally claimed that, among cells with feature_024 <= -7.353, outcome_015 in feature_048 level_001 is more negative than in level_003. Discovery was significantly opposite that claim: the signed estimate was -0.042, meaning the raw level_001 minus level_003 contrast was about +0.042, i.e. level_001 was less negative, weaker dependency. The scheduled validation then gave +0.024 signed to the original direction, with independent interval [-0.017, +0.064], crossing zero and much smaller than the discovery opposite effect. Thus H181 is rejected because neither the original direction nor a stable opposite stratum-specific effect is supported. The linked reversed proposal H185 captured the raw-positive discovery contrast but failed validation: its validation estimate is -0.024 signed to the reversed direction, independent interval [-0.064, +0.017], again null/opposite. Reject and close H185. The related H182 interaction remained only nominally significant in discovery and depended on the stratum asymmetry now invalidated; because direct interaction evidence is not independently validated and effect-modification claims are multiplicity-prone, it should not be accepted. Leave H182 formally unresolved but close the investigation as deprioritized, not supported. Overall, there are no accepted claims. The dataset-specific negative evidence is substantial: broad screens, categorical contrasts, common binary predictors, feature_057 dose contrasts, feature_045 leads, feature_034/feature_002/feature_060 interactions, feature_028 levels, and now feature_048 stratum tests have produced mostly null, imprecise, subclinical, reversed, or non-replicated associations. Some unresolved uncertainty remains because validation intervals can be wide, several deferred contrasts were never tested, and nominal subclinical effects such as H182 could reflect real but small heterogeneity; however, none meets the evidence bar for scientifically meaningful association. The most informative next analysis would not be further post-hoc predictor mining. If resources continue, the highest-value analysis is a prespecified, well-powered test of a new biologically motivated predictor or a calibration/negative-control workflow to estimate the false-positive and attenuation behavior of this multiplicity-rich discovery-validation process. Generalizability and causality are not claimed.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

record.narrative: No assessments are due. I am running the six active prespecified subtype-screening claims H186-H191, plus four registered deferred contrasts that complete the same feature_055/feature_063 categorical families: H45, H46, H122, and H124. This gives a focused triangulation rather than a new broad predictor sweep. Feature_055 is attractive because its levels are well powered: level_004 versus level_001 or level_003 contrasts have roughly several hundred observations per cell, and level_002 versus level_001 provides an intermediate-level check. Feature_063 level_003 versus level_001 has a sufficiently sized exposed cell and can be assessed across multiple dependency outcomes. All selected claims use direction -1; therefore a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has the hypothesized more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency. The key scientific bar is a clinically meaningful relative difference, approximately 10% of the absolute outcome mean for most dependency scores (about 0.025-0.03 score units for outcomes with means near -0.25 to -0.30, and smaller for outcome_014). Acceptance would require a point estimate at or above that scale and an interval that is not dominated by null or opposite values. If this panel is null, opposite, or subclinical, it will close the last well-powered categorical predictor families and further support the broader dataset-specific conclusion that no measured predictor or subgroup comparison has robustly shown a clinically meaningful association. These are association tests only, without causal or generalization claims.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All due results complete the well-powered categorical feature_055 and feature_063 screening panel. The estimates are already signed to the registered direction (-1): a positive value means the raw contrast is in the hypothesized more-negative/stronger-dependency direction, while a negative value means the raw contrast is opposite that hypothesis. None of the claimed associations reaches the scientific/clinical bar of roughly a 10% absolute-mean-scale difference in these dependency scores. H186 and H45 are both positive for outcome_013 feature_055 contrasts but have point estimates only about +0.018 and +0.012, below the outcome_013 10% proxy of roughly 0.027, with intervals including zero, opposite values, and uncertainty compatible with subclinical effects. H187 and H188 are negative/small, again not supporting the hypothesized direction. H189 and H190 are essentially null, with estimates near zero and wide intervals that provide no support for feature_055 level_004 versus level_001 or feature_063 level_003 versus level_001 on outcome_016. H191 and H46 are the closest to a clinically sized effect, but they are opposite to the registered direction and still only subclinical relative to their outcome-specific 10% proxies (roughly -0.025 for outcome_008 and -0.026 for outcome_013). Their intervals are wide, include zero and the claimed direction, and the exposed level_003 cell is small (n=98), so these nominal opposite point estimates are fragile. They also do not form a coherent pattern: H122 and H124 for feature_063 level_003 versus level_001 on other outcomes are null, and H190 is null. Given the large number of post-hoc predictor and outcome comparisons, the absence of internally consistent clinically sized effects, and the fact that no interval provides strong evidence for the claimed direction beyond threshold, I reject and close these claims. No independent validation is requested: none of these remaining active claims is sufficiently promising, internally consistent, or close enough to the clinical threshold to justify spending one of the remaining validation samples, especially because the rare feature_063 level would produce wide independent intervals and likely low power. These conclusions are limited to this supplied dataset and do not establish causality or generalizability.

Iteration 14/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.
