You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response

the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

record.narrative: I assessed the six new discovery results against a 10%-of-absolute-mean clinical proxy. For outcome_009, the absolute mean is about 0.256, so the practical threshold is about 0.0256. H240 is the strongest new stratified evidence: the signed positive level_001-vs-level_003 difference is 0.0334, about 13% of the absolute mean, with an entirely positive interval, but its lower bound is 0.0062, below the clinical proxy. Therefore it is suggestive and clinically sized at the point estimate, but not sufficient to accept a scientifically meaningful difference with adequate uncertainty. I leave H240 unresolved and active. H241 has a signed estimate of 0.0250, slightly below the 10% proxy, with an interval including zero and opposite-direction differences; it is inconclusive and low priority, so I leave it unresolved and deferred rather than accept it. The main H239 positive outcome_009 contrast remains active because its overall signed estimate of 0.0291 is above the proxy and the two feature_024 strata have positive point estimates, but the lower bound is still below the proxy, the feature_024 split was post-hoc in the broader feature_048 family, and the multiple-comparison burden remains large. I therefore keep H239 unresolved and request independent validation for H239: it is the broadest, least subgroup-selected version of the currently most coherent positive lead, and validation can test whether the level_001-vs-level_003 association is stable rather than a discovery-sample or multiplicity artifact. For the feature_032/feature_046 probes on outcome_014 and outcome_006, the absolute-mean proxy is about 0.0093 because those outcomes have large variance and near-zero means. H242 is striking: a signed estimate of 0.0685 corresponds to about 74% of the absolute mean, but its lower bound is slightly negative (-0.0012), the exposed cell is only 110, and the result is a borderline rare-group finding after broad outcome screening. I cannot accept it or use it to override uncertainty, so I mark it unresolved and deferred. H243 is tiny and imprecise; I reject and close it. H244 is also imprecise and opposite the registered direction, so the registered claim is rejected and closed; the opposite signal is not stable enough to justify a post-hoc reverse claim. H245 has a very large signed point estimate, about 43% of the absolute mean, but its interval includes zero and clinically large opposite differences, so it is inconclusive and deferred. Overall, no new claim supports a scientifically meaningful association with adequate directional and clinical precision, and no claim is accepted from this batch. All conclusions are dataset-specific and noncausal; the validation request is intended only to assess stability of the outcome_009 feature_048 lead.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative:
The new independent validation for H239 resolves the outcome_009 feature_048 lead against a scientifically meaningful positive exposed-minus-comparator association. The discovery result R223 was nominally positive in the registered direction: signed estimate +0.0291, 95% CI +0.0093 to +0.0489. For outcome_009, the practical 10%-of-absolute-mean threshold is about 0.0256, so the point estimate exceeded the threshold but the lower confidence bound was only about 3.6% of the absolute mean and therefore clinically imprecise. The independent validation R250 reversed direction and was small: signed estimate -0.0052, validation-adjusted interval -0.0345 to +0.0241. That provides no support for a stable positive difference, and it directly contradicts the discovery lead in sign. I therefore reject H239 and close it. H218 remains rejected, and the feature_024-stratified outcome_009 leads H240 and H241 are not worth keeping active because their parent broad contrast failed independent validation and their discovery lower bounds were also below the clinical threshold.

The overall supported findings remain null: no measured predictor or subgroup has robustly demonstrated a scientifically meaningful association with any of the 16 CRISPR dependency outcomes in this dataset. Broad and focused screens of binary and categorical predictors, including feature_034, feature_002, feature_060, feature_054, feature_028, feature_055, feature_019, feature_048, feature_063, feature_045, feature_042, feature_020, feature_021, feature_022, feature_037, feature_050, feature_052, feature_008, feature_047, feature_023, feature_064, and feature_057, yielded mostly null, subclinical, directionally unstable, or validation-inconsistent results. Many nominal discovery leads failed independent validation, including feature_048/outcome_009, feature_048/feature_024/outcome_015 low-feature_024 contrasts, feature_020/outcome_006, feature_057/outcome_012, and feature_065 contrasts. These conclusions are dataset-specific, descriptive, noncausal, and not claims about generalizability.

The main unresolved uncertainty is now H242, feature_032 versus outcome_014. The registered negative-direction claim has discovery evidence R246 with signed magnitude +0.0685, corresponding to a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference of approximately -0.0685, with 95% CI in signed coordinates -0.0012 to +0.1381. Outcome_014 has a small absolute mean, so the 10%-of-absolute-mean proxy is about 0.0093; the point estimate is enormous relative to that threshold, but the lower bound crosses zero and the exposed cell is rare (n=110), so this is an important but unstable high-magnitude lead. I have promoted H242 to active priority because, if one remaining independent validation request is available, it is the most informative use of that budget: it tests a simple predictor, has the largest unresolved clinical-scale point estimate, and a failure would further support the null conclusion across rare high-variance outcome probes. H182 is retained only as a deferred secondary lead because it is a post-hoc feature_048/feature_024 interaction with a lower bound below the outcome_015 clinical proxy and because the broader feature_048 family has repeatedly failed validation. H245 remains deferred and less compelling. The feature_009 level_002-versus-level_003 tests remain unresolved only because of inadequate cell sizes, not because of evidence for an effect. The next analysis should therefore be a targeted prespecified validation of H242, with acceptance requiring stable direction and uncertainty bounds that support a clinically meaningful difference; if that validation fails, the final evidence supports no scientifically meaningful predictor or subgroup associations in this dataset.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: New validation for H242 changes the scientific conclusion for the feature_032 - outcome_014 lead from unresolved to rejected. The claim is registered in the negative exposed-minus-comparator direction, so positive signed values correspond to a more negative dependency score in feature_032=1 versus feature_032=0. Discovery R246 gave signed estimate +0.0685, corresponding to a raw exposed-minus-comparator mean difference of approximately -0.0685, with 95% Welch interval -0.0012 to +0.1381 and only 110 exposed cases. Outcome_014 has a small absolute mean, making the 10%-of-absolute-mean clinical proxy about 0.0093, so the point estimate was very large relative to that proxy, but the interval crossed zero and included clinically meaningful values of both signs. Independent validation R255 instead gave signed estimate +0.0042, raw approximately -0.0042, with validation-adjusted interval -0.1069 to +0.1153 and 105 exposed cases. This is small relative to the clinical proxy, does not have a clinically meaningful lower bound, and remains directionally unstable because the interval admits large effects of either sign. Therefore I reject H242 and close it. I also reject H246 because the rare low-feature_024 subgroup lead is not supported by the independent overall validation and its discovery lower bound was only just above zero and far below the clinical proxy. H247, H248, and H249 remain closed; H245 is rejected because its interval includes zero. H182 remains unresolved but is closed as an active lead because it is a post-hoc interaction with a lower bound below the clinical threshold and no remaining validation budget. Overall, no measured predictor or subgroup has demonstrated a scientifically meaningful association with any of the 16 CRISPR dependency outcomes in this dataset. The supported conclusion is negative and dataset-specific: across broad screens and focused follow-ups, nominal discovery leads failed independent validation, reversed direction, or remained too imprecise to meet the 10% relative-difference standard. This does not exclude small effects, stratum-specific effects in other datasets, or causal effects. The most informative future analysis is a prespecified independent validation or well-powered test of the remaining nominal feature_048 level_001 versus level_003 interaction with feature_024 for outcome_015, plus well-powered sparse feature_009 level_002 versus level_003 tests; no further validation can be requested within this run.

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.

Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

status (accept/reject/unresolved),

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Final synthesis: The newly delivered independent validation for H239, evidence R250, rejects the claim that feature_048 level_001 versus level_003 has a clinically meaningful positive-direction association with outcome_009 in this dataset. H239 is the reverse-direction claim for outcome_009, feature_048 level_001 versus level_003. Discovery R223 produced a nominal signed effect of +0.0291 with 95% Welch interval +0.0093 to +0.0489. For outcome_009, whose absolute mean is about 0.256, the 10 percent relative-difference clinical proxy is approximately 0.0256. The point estimate exceeded that proxy, but the interval lower bound was below it, so discovery alone did not establish a clinically meaningful effect. Independent validation R250 is decisive: the signed estimate is -0.0052, interval -0.0345 to +0.0241, with a validation-adjusted alpha. The validation point estimate is small and opposite the claimed direction, the interval includes zero and clinically opposite effects, and its upper bound is below the clinical proxy. Therefore H239 is not supported and is closed. The same R250 evidence, viewed through the opposite H218 direction, likewise fails: it is near zero, imprecise, and includes zero. This closes the main-effect feature_048 level_001 versus level_003 signal for outcome_009 as unsupported by independent validation.

The broader supported conclusion remains negative and dataset-specific: across the 16 CRISPR dependency outcomes, no measured predictor or subgroup has demonstrated a robust, scientifically meaningful, clinically meaningful association. Many discovery leads that looked promising were either rejected because intervals included zero, rejected because independent validation reversed direction or shrank toward null, rejected because effect bounds were not compatible with the 10 percent clinical threshold, or left unresolved because they were post-hoc, rare, or underpowered and validation budget is exhausted. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: I audited the eight newly delivered discovery tests as a pre-specified completeness panel for three balanced binary predictors, not as post-hoc screening. The Welch diagnostics are valid and every comparison cell is large: feature_034 cells are 1039/961, feature_002 cells are 989/1011, and feature_060 cells are 1004/996. The returned intervals are signed to the registered negative-dependency direction, so positive signed values favor more negative dependency in the exposed group, while negative signed values favor the opposite direction. To judge clinical/scientific importance, I used the same 10% absolute-mean proxy as previous assessments: approximately 0.0269 for outcome_013, 0.0250 for outcome_015, 0.0255 for outcome_004, 0.0250 for outcome_005, 0.0245 for outcome_007, and 0.0256 for outcome_016. These are descriptive marginal comparisons, so residual confounding by correlated measured variables remains possible, and no causal interpretation is warranted. H253 rejects: feature_034=1 versus 0 for outcome_013 has a signed estimate of -0.0187, with interval -0.0385 to +0.0012, opposite the claimed direction, below the clinical threshold, and compatible with no effect. H254 is the only borderline signal: feature_034=1 versus 0 for outcome_015 has signed estimate +0.0170 and interval +0.0017 to +0.0323. In raw exposed-minus-comparator terms this is a small negative mean difference of about -0.0170, or roughly 6.8% of the absolute outcome mean, below the 10% clinical threshold. Although the signed interval excludes zero, the lower bound is far below clinical relevance and the upper bound only barely exceeds it; with the full-run multiplicity burden and no remaining validation budget, this does not justify accepting a scientifically meaningful association. I therefore reject the clinically meaningful claim for H254 while preserving the nuance that a small nominal negative mean difference exists in this dataset. H255, H257, and H259 reject: feature_002 and feature_060 effects on outcome_004 or outcome_007 are small, signed intervals include zero, and none approaches the clinical threshold. H256, H258, and H260 reject: the signed point estimates are opposite the claimed direction and the intervals include zero or clinically opposite effects, again far below threshold. Validation is not requested because the independent-validation budget is exhausted and none of these results is robust enough to justify spending an unavailable slot. No new proposal is warranted; these completeness results strengthen the dataset-specific descriptive conclusion that there is no robust evidence for clinically meaningful measured-predictor associations with the 16 CRISPR dependency scores.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
Response deadline addressed for H242. The independent validation evidence R255 decisively rejects the claim that feature_032=1 versus feature_032=0 is associated with a scientifically meaningful more negative outcome_014 dependency score. H242 was registered with direction -1, so a positive signed estimate represents raw exposed-minus-comparator evidence in the claimed direction, namely a more negative outcome in feature_032=1. Validation R255 gives a signed estimate of only +0.0042, with a validation-adjusted interval from -0.1069 to +0.1153. Using the absolute mean of outcome_014, about 0.093, as the denominator for the 10% relative clinical proxy, the threshold is approximately 0.0093. The validation point estimate is below this proxy, and the interval includes zero, clinically opposite effects, and wide regions in both directions. Therefore the independent data do not support the claimed association. This matters because discovery R246 had produced a nominally larger signed estimate of +0.0685, interval -0.0012 to +0.1381, in a rare exposure group of 110 versus 1890 observations. That discovery interval already crossed zero and was unstable because of the small exposed cell; the independent validation shrank the point estimate toward null and widened the uncertainty, so H242 is best treated as a negative dataset-specific finding. I therefore assess H242 as rejected and closed.

Final scientific report. Across the full investigation of 16 CRISPR dependency outcomes and many measured binary, numeric, and categorical predictors, the evidence does not support any robust, scientifically or clinically meaningful predictor or subgroup association in this supplied dataset. The most important supported scientific conclusion is negative and descriptive: after broad screening, focused follow-up, and independent validation, no tested comparison has yielded a reproducible effect compatible with the 10% relative-difference clinical threshold. Most main-effect and interaction results had intervals that included zero, point estimates far below clinical relevance, or validation results that reversed direction, collapsed toward null, or remained too imprecise.

Supported findings: none of the tested directional association claims is accepted as a robust scientifically meaningful difference in CRISPR dependency score after the full discovery and validation record. Many results are informative as negative findings, but they support the absence of detectable association in this dataset, not universal absence or causal nullity.

Negative findings: numerous predictor-outcome comparisons across feature_034, feature_002, feature_060, feature_048, feature_055, feature_028, feature_019, feature_057, feature_020, feature_045, feature_065, feature_063, feature_032, and others are rejected or closed. Several initially suggestive nominal signals were deflated or contradicted by validation, including feature_048 main effects for outcome_009 and outcome_015-related subgroup signals, feature_020 for outcome_006, feature_057 comparisons for outcome_012, feature_065 effects for outcome_015, and feature_032 for outcome_014. The H242 validation response is part of this negative pattern: a rare-group discovery signal did not replicate.

Unresolved uncertainty: some exploratory signals remain closed as unresolved or insufficiently powered because validation budget is exhausted. The most notable are post-hoc feature_048-related signals: H182, a feature_048 by feature_024 interaction for outcome_015; H240 and H241, feature_024-stratified feature_048 effects for outcome_009; and sparse-cell comparisons involving feature_009 level_002 versus level_003, including H83, H84, H123, and H125. These should not be treated as accepted findings. Their discovery intervals either include zero, have lower bounds below the clinical threshold, involve rare cells, or are too exploratory to validate within the current evidence budget. H254 is also worth noting as a small nominal feature_034 effect for outcome_015, but it is subclinical relative to the 10% proxy and not robust enough to change the overall conclusion.

Causality and generalizability: all accepted or rejected conclusions are descriptive associations within the supplied dataset. The opaque predictor labels and correlated measured variables mean residual confounding and biological mechanism remain unresolved. No causal interpretation is justified. Generalizability beyond this dataset is uncertain, and the negative results should be read as failure to detect robust associations under the current testing design, not as proof that no such predictors exist in the broader biological system.

record.narrative: No new scientifically useful comparisons are registered. The investigation has exhausted the most informative discovery avenues: balanced binary predictors have been comprehensively screened across the 16 CRISPR dependency outcomes; focused follow-up and independent validation have repeatedly failed to support a reproducible, clinically meaningful association. The remaining unresolved leads are not amenable to valid new discovery tests in this dataset: feature_048/feature_024 signals require a prespecified, adequately powered independent replication with a fixed cutoff and multiplicity control; feature_009 level_002 versus level_003 comparisons have insufficient cell size under the minimum 20 observations per cell; and other post-hoc subgroup screens would increase false-positive risk without a clear prior. Because the independent validation budget is also exhausted, registering additional hypotheses would mainly serve post-hoc exploration rather than improve the scientific evidence. The final dataset-specific conclusion remains that no measured predictor or subgroup has been shown to have a robust, clinically meaningful association with any of the 16 CRISPR dependency scores. These findings are descriptive associations in the supplied dataset and do not establish causal effects or broader generalizability.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
